entries.operation: CNB's loader registry, and the native content manager it needs
entries.evidence: measured rather than deferred on style. The registry itself works: a C probe mints a custom asset type id from a name, registers a loader, writes a .cnb of that type, and cna_content_manager_load_foreign_ext calls the loader and hands the object back -- twice for the same name, from the cache, without calling the loader again, which is XNA reference-type caching. What blocks the projection is this binding's own architecture: that retrieval route takes a NATIVE content manager handle, and there is none here. ContentManager in this package is a managed XNB reader that opens the file through TitleContainer and constructs the object in TypeScript, and no cna_content_manager_* route is imported at all. Registering a loader whose product could never be retrieved would be a mechanism with no consumer. Adopting it means projecting CNA's own ContentManager as a second content path with its own cache, which is an architectural decision to take deliberately rather than as a side effect of wanting one registry. The callback shape is not the obstacle: a trampoline holding a napi_ref and a checked slot table would keep void* and function pointers entirely inside the bridge, the same way the text-input subscriptions already do

entries.operation: Modern CNA engine layer beyond the pipeline, the post-process chain, compute, clustered lighting, LOD, shadow-map maths and particles: the shadow and particle draw passes, decals and atmospheric rendering

What is left is the two draw passes -- a shadow map's depth pass and a particle system's draw -- plus cascaded, spot and cube shadow maps, decals, light probes and atmospheric rendering. Both draw passes are deliberately unprojected rather than merely unwritten: each needs a real render pass, and the one renderer here that could run one answers every render-target readback with zeros (upstream finding 7), so there would be no evidence to accept them on

entries.operation: The camera use-after-free CNA has today
entries.evidence: destroying a test-backend camera and then opening the platform one is a segmentation fault in CNA 0.21.0: the C ABI installs the test provider as a process-wide platform override holding a raw pointer into the camera resource, and cna_camera_destroy frees that resource without clearing the override. Reproduced in plain C with no binding involved, backtrace resolved to CNA::Devices::Camera::Camera at Camera.cpp:68. cna-ts runs the crashing sequence in a child process and asserts the child dies, so a repair fails the test rather than passing unnoticed; every probe here that opens the platform camera runs before the first test-backend one

entries.operation: Build-time content compilation: source files into .cnb, in a separate package
entries.evidence: The direction docs/content-pipeline-boundary.md chose, built. `cna-ts-content` is a separate package with its own exports, and the runtime tarball contains none of it: the three routes in the whole binding that read a file by path live there and nowhere else, which is what keeps the browser runtime free of filesystem and compiler APIs. Bytes cross that boundary and handles do not -- each operation imports, describes, encodes and releases inside one native call -- so the package owns no native lifetime at all. Proved end to end: a PNG and a RIFF/WAVE file written from their own specifications (not produced by CNA, because an importer test in which CNA reads back its own output proves nothing) are compiled to .cnb, written to disk, and loaded by the real runtime, where the four exact texels and the exact sample bytes come back. The colour key is asserted at the texel: the keyed one becomes transparent and the other three are untouched. Wrong-format sources are refused in both directions, and a planted defect that accepted the colour key without applying it passed until the test stopped varying the content name as well

entries.operation: Camera frame capture
entries.evidence: opening the platform camera succeeds on a host that has none -- CNA documented contract -- and the state is what reports the absence: NotSupported with a 0x0 frame format. CNA own test backend then supplies what the hardware cannot: four distinct pixels published through it arrive in a caller-owned Texture2D with their channels the right way round, a second frame of sixteen different bytes replaces the first, a texture whose size does not match the frame is refused rather than resized, and the frame stays available until it is replaced. Every injectable state round-trips, and CNA refuses Closed and NotSupported for a device it opened. The injection hooks refuse a camera that is not the test backend, so a test cannot fabricate a reading for a real device. Three planted defects -- zeroed pixels, an acquisition that always claims success, and hooks that accept a real camera -- all fail. This is injection evidence, not hardware evidence: a physical camera stays hardware-pending

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the assignment a GPU would read
entries.evidence: the three views of one assignment -- the per-cluster read, the flat index list and the per-cluster offsets -- are checked against each other for every one of sixty-four clusters, not a sample. The final offset equals the index list length equals the reported total reference count, the offsets never go backwards, and the reported maximum lights per cluster is the largest cluster actually produced. A per-cluster read that ignored its argument and an offset list missing its end marker were both planted and both fail

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the cluster grid's exact geometry
entries.evidence: all sixty-four clusters of a 4x2x8 grid, each flat index checked against slice * tilesX * tilesY + y * tilesX + x rather than a sample. The depth axis is logarithmic and asserted against the closed form near * (far/near)^(slice/count), and separately asserted not to be the linear spacing, which would otherwise satisfy every weaker check. The projection round-trips: multiplying it by the inverse CNA returns gives the identity to within 1e-5 through XNA own Matrix.Multiply. A planted x/y swap in the index mapping fails this

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the light set and what CNA refuses to light with
entries.evidence: three lights with three different values in every field, added, read back one at a time and in bulk, replaced, removed and cleared. A point light influence is a sphere on its own position with its own range; a spot influence is its cone bounding sphere, which is somewhere else entirely, and that difference is what shows CNA computing the bounds rather than copying the position -- a planted position-and-range substitution fails it. The two add paths are cross-checked: a point light added through CNA own conversion agrees with the same light built in the uniform shape on every field that has an effect and on the computed bounds, and differs only in the direction and cone angles a point light does not have, which CNA fills with its own canonical defaults rather than zero -- a rule this package hands to CNA rather than restating. CNA refuses a zero or negative range, a negative intensity and a spot whose inner angle is wider than its outer, each with INVALID_ARGUMENT

entries.operation: Clustered lighting: the shadow budget, and the refusals it counts
entries.evidence: two of three lights ask for a shadow map because only two carry the flag, so the request count is a property of the scene rather than of the budget. A budget of one grants one and counts one refusal; a budget of zero grants nothing and refuses every request. IsSelected and GetSelected name the same lights, a selected light has a positive score, and the hysteresis margin round-trips

entries.operation: CNA sensors: support enumeration and the accelerometer's absence path

Start, Stop and the update interval report what the platform did rather than what was asked, disposal is idempotent, and a released sensor does not block the next one

entries.operation: CNB container: parse, validate, walk the table of contents and read chunk bytes
entries.evidence: a container encoded by CNA's own writer parses back with its container version, asset type, schema version, CMET metadata and chunk order; a chunk's bytes are exact and its CRC-32C recomputes to the table-of-contents value; truncation, a flipped payload byte and an XNB are each refused with CNA_RESULT_IO, and an unknown mandatory chunk refuses the whole file

entries.operation: CNB curves and animation clips
entries.evidence: A curve round-trips its two loop modes, its key count and every field of every key, including a continuity that differs between keys -- and then it is checked the way a curve actually matters, by evaluating both the authored and the decoded curve at ten positions including four between the keys, where the tangents and the continuity decide the answer. What comes back is a managed XNA Curve with no native object behind it: the native handle and its key collection are both released inside the decode. An animation clip keeps its handle, because XNA has no clip type to become; its duration, target space, two tracks with different bone indexes and different keyframe counts, and every component of every keyframe -- three vectors of different lengths at different offsets -- are asserted, along with out-of-range refusals and the fact that a curve and a clip refuse each other's containers. Two planted bridge defects, a dropped key continuity and an ignored track index, each fail exactly one test

entries.operation: CNB model: the bone hierarchy, parts and payloads, materials, meshes, skeleton and lights
entries.evidence: CNB's largest schema, read and written through CnbModelData. A reference model with every projected level occupied at once -- two bones in a hierarchy, a part with real vertex and index payloads, a material with distinguishable values in every field and all eight texture slots named differently, a mesh, a skeleton with three matrix sets, a light -- is built with the public API, encoded by CNA's own writer and decoded back. Every assertion is a value: the exact parent links and transforms, the exact payload bytes and lengths, each of the eight texture names through its own slot, the mesh's parent bone and part membership, and all three skeleton matrix sets kept apart by their own diagonals. Refusals are asserted too: another asset type, a corrupted image, a payload that contradicts its declared part (which CNA validates at encode rather than at set, measured rather than assumed), and use after disposal. Two planted bridge defects -- an ignored skeleton matrix-set identity and an ignored texture slot -- each fail exactly one test

entries.operation: CNB sound effects, songs and videos: the compiled media schemas
entries.evidence: A sound effect round-trips its format, rate, channels, frame count, both loop numbers and its sample bytes exactly, and CNA's own WAV decoder reads a RIFF image into one with the same bytes the header declared; a file that is not a WAV is refused. CreateSoundEffectFromCnb produces a real XNA SoundEffect owning a native audio resource whose name round-trips through CNA, and refuses by name for a format XNA cannot represent -- eight-bit PCM read as sixteen would play as noise -- while leaving the samples readable. Songs and videos carry a stream reference rather than the media, so both schemas are complete and fully testable with no encoded audio or video at all: name, duration and stream reference for a song; dimensions, a non-integer frame rate, duration, soundtrack kind and stream reference for a video. Each of the three refuses the other two's containers. Duration is zero on this artifact because it is built with CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=NULL, which is a property of the configuration rather than of the schema; the real 250 ms measurement is made in the browser suite, whose artifact has SDL3 audio

entries.operation: CNB SpriteFont: decode a compiled font with its embedded atlas into a drawable SpriteFont
entries.evidence: a font CNA encoded decodes with its metrics, its ascending character map and its per-glyph rectangles and kerning; CreateSpriteFontFromCnb builds a SpriteFont whose MeasureString is exact, the copied atlas outlives the font it came from, an unsorted character map is refused at encode time, and an absent fallback character reads as null rather than U+0000

entries.operation: CNB Texture2D: decode a compiled texture and upload it as a real XNA resource
entries.evidence: a texture description CNA encoded decodes to the same shape, representation format and level bytes, and CreateTexture2DFromCnb produces a Texture2D whose four readback texels are exactly the RGBA the encoder was given; representation selection reports an unsupported format as absence rather than failure

entries.operation: CNB's writers: authoring a container for an asset type CNA has no schema for
entries.evidence: one of every primitive the byte writer offers, decoded back at its exact offset with a DataView -- which is what proves the widths and the little-endian order rather than only that some bytes survived. A u64 survives exactly because it crosses as a bigint; a negative i32 is not read as unsigned; a string carries a four-byte length before its UTF-8 bytes. ToArray copies and Take empties, and the two are distinct. A container built from a custom asset type, custom schema version, metadata, an external reference and a game-defined chunk parses back through the same CnbDocument reader every projected schema uses, with the chunk payload byte for byte. CNB validates structure when a chunk is added -- alignment must be a power of two within its ceiling -- and sizes when the document is built, and both halves are asserted where they happen. Four planted defects all fail: a Take that copies, a u16 written at 32 bits, a dropped power-of-two check, and a limit narrowed but never sent

entries.operation: Compass and motion sensors: absence, and a real reading through CNA's own injection
entries.evidence: Absence first, and it is the point of the family: a heading of zero and a rotation rate of zero are both perfectly plausible measurements, so all three sensors report NotSupported with no valid data and refuse CurrentValue rather than returning them. Then the data path, through cna_compass_set_test_backend_ext and cna_motion_set_test_backend_ext -- CNA's own synthetic backends -- which is **injection evidence, not hardware evidence**: no physical compass or motion sensor exists on this host. Every component carries a value no other component has, so a transposed or substituted field is visible: two compass headings that differ by the local declination, a magnetometer vector, a 16-value attitude matrix asserted by first row and diagonal, a quaternion, and three motion vectors with disjoint value sets. Timestamps cross as bigints and are asserted to the tick, which a double would lose. The north-reference flag is installed both ways and read back both ways, so it is proved read rather than defaulted. A backend cannot be swapped underneath a running acquisition. Three planted defects each fail the test: two headings read from one field, a transposed attitude matrix, and gravity read from the device acceleration

entries.operation: Compiled Effect creation binding route
entries.evidence: exact byte payload reaches cna_effect_create_compiled with compiler-verified ABI; three legal conformance-FXB attempts deterministically return the qualified HEADLESS result 6 with invalid output and no shader-execution claim

entries.operation: Compute shaders and storage buffers: exact GPU computation
entries.evidence: a dispatch computes values[i] * uScale + uOffset + i over 64 float elements, and all four inputs are separately load-bearing: every element differs, so a dispatch that did nothing leaves the seed, one that ignored either uniform produces a different sequence, and one that ignored the invocation index produces a constant. Two work groups of sixteen touch exactly the first thirty-two elements, which is what proves the dispatch count reaches the GPU. Measured on OPENGLES3 under Xvfb; HEADLESS, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE refuse every create with NOT_SUPPORTED and that refusal is asserted rather than skipped. A typed buffer refuses an element transfer whose element size disagrees with its own

entries.operation: Direct standalone GraphicsDevice construction
entries.evidence: XNA public GraphicsDevice constructor now creates a real second device beside the game one, with no game of its own: cna_graphics_device_create takes an adapter index and presentation parameters and nothing else. A Texture2D made on it round-trips its four exact texels, its viewport and presentation parameters are its own rather than the manager (64x48 against the game 320x240), two caller-created devices live at once each answering with its own profile and size, and a texture from one device is refused by another device SpriteBatch with InvalidOperationException. The ownership rule is asserted directly off the native lifetime rather than inferred from a symptom: a caller-created device releases its own handle exactly once, and disposing a manager-created device leaves the game native lifetime active -- a Dispose that released whatever lifetime it found passed every other assertion and is caught only by that one. The adapter index is the adapter own position in CNA enumeration, which one physical adapter cannot discriminate, so test/standalone-device.test.mjs supplies two deterministic adapters and proves the index and the reported adapter are both the given one

entries.operation: Extended input: raw joysticks and force feedback, on a host with neither attached
entries.evidence: cna-ts/extensions/input is a new public subpath, kept out of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Input deliberately: a joystick's axes are raw, its identity is the platform's GUID, and it may carry hats and trackballs GamePadState has no member for, so folding one into the XNA type would drop data or invent a mapping. What this host proves is the absence contract, and CNA's is consistent and worth pinning -- measured rather than assumed. An identifier no device has is not refused; it is answered *absent*: a disconnected descriptor with zero counts and an empty name and GUID, which is the convention XNA's own GamePad.GetCapabilities follows. The haptic half is the stronger claim -- opening an absent device produces one that reports itself closed, offers no features, and declines InitializeRumble, PlayRumble, StopRumble and SetGain rather than silently accepting a request it cannot perform, which would be worse than an exception because a game would then offer the setting. Disposal closes and releases in that order, once

entries.evidence: native lifecycle and dynamic/media pump integration

entries.evidence: qualified ABI-0.7 integration covers seven real game lifetimes and 60/600 frames

entries.operation: GamerServicesDispatcher lifetime and Guide state over real CNA gamer services
entries.evidence: the dispatcher initialises against the running game and reports CNA's own IsInitialized rather than a mirrored flag; a 64-bit platform window handle round-trips as a bigint; Guide's trial-mode simulation, notification position and visibility read and write through CNA. Two XNA rules CNA does not enforce are enforced here and asserted: an un-initialised Update raises InvalidOperationException, and IsTrialMode is the disjunction with SimulateTrialMode. IsScreenSaverEnabled is a platform display property, so with no displays the getter answers true and a write does not take -- reported rather than cached. Nothing fabricates a gamer: SignedInGamers is empty and every screen-showing operation still refuses with GamerServicesNotAvailableException

entries.operation: GameWindow stable facade, borrowed handle/state and removable event registrations
entries.evidence: qualified integration verifies stable Game.Window identity, zero HEADLESS handle, title/state queries, callback registration cleanup and repeated game lifetimes

entries.operation: GPU timers: a measured frame duration
entries.evidence: a non-blocking timer query wrapped around one real frame of drawing and polled on later frames, collecting a sub-millisecond measurement on OPENGLES3 with exactly one sample. A timer creates even where the renderer has no timer query at all, which is CNA reporting the absence through the object rather than by refusing: on HEADLESS it answers IsSupported false and names the missing GL extension in CNA own words

entries.operation: GraphicsAdapter: the adapter list, its display modes and its format answers
entries.evidence: The one strict XNA type this package projected structurally and could not fill, because nothing read CNA's adapter capabilities. Its fourteen routes are now bound and the type is real on HEADLESS and on three windowed renderers. The read is deliberately lazy: CNA's adapter routes take a *borrowed* graphics-device handle and permit that borrow only inside a lifecycle callback, so a read at device-creation time is refused with INVALID_STATE -- what is registered there is a source, resolved the first time a caller asks, which for a game is from LoadContent. Asserted: one adapter, its four separate integer identity fields, a current display mode whose aspect ratio matches its own dimensions, a supported-mode list, both XNA profiles with HiDef implying Reach, and a 64x multisample request answered inexactly with a count CNA can actually provide. The description and device name are CNA's canonical XNA values rather than a GPU probe -- the same on HEADLESS and OPENGLES3 -- and that is stated rather than dressed up. A renderer with no adapters still refuses by name; a renderer with no native monitor handle answers zero, which is a legal IntPtr, rather than failing the whole adapter. Three planted defects fail it, including one that only fails because the test compares a case where the back-buffer and render-target queries genuinely disagree: Reach + Single is refused as a back buffer and accepted as a render target

entries.operation: GraphicsDevice bound, indexed, instanced and four-codec user draw dispatch
entries.evidence: 360-symbol bridge dispatch and argument layouts are signature-audited; qualified HEADLESS calls reach CNA; no visible-output claim

entries.operation: GraphicsDevice capability query and the compute work-group limits
entries.evidence: XNA had GraphicsProfile, a two-value tier standing in for a capability list; CNA answers per capability and cna-ts asks rather than assumes. All nineteen answers are cross-checked against the renderer own capability bitmask, which reaches the test through a different route, on three windowed renderers whose masks differ (OPENGLES3 0x7ffff, SOFTWARE 0x1af7, SDL_RENDERER 0x1000) and on HEADLESS, which answers ten of nineteen. That the bitmask form is one shifted by the ordinal form is a compile-time fact rather than an assumption: tools/cna-abi/contract.json asserts it for all nineteen

entries.operation: Level-of-detail groups, and the hysteresis that damps a boundary
entries.evidence: levels added out of order come back sorted, and every band is checked on both sides of every threshold -- a threshold ends its level, and past the last one the answer is -1 rather than a clamp to the coarsest. The hysteresis is the part worth proving: with a margin of 3 around a boundary at 25, climbing holds the near level until 28 and descending holds the far one until 22, and the two walks are asserted not to be each other reversed, which is what separates hysteresis from rounding. A jump of more than one level is deliberately undamped, and that is asserted too. Screen-space selection projects radius * (height / 2) / (distance * tan(fov / 2)) exactly, and halving with distance. Three planted defects fail: a Reset that does not forget, a margin that never reaches CNA, and a projection that ignores its distance. CNA associates each level with a ModelMeshPart and can hand it back; that half is deliberately unprojected because this package ModelMeshPart is managed and has no native handle to give, so the route could only ever answer nothing

entries.operation: Shadow-map maths: what a quality tier costs, and where a light looks from
entries.evidence: the quality ladder is asserted both as its exact five values (512/512/1024/2048/4096 and filter radii 0/0/1/2/2) and as a property -- monotonic, and Ultra strictly larger than Disabled -- so a renumbering that kept the same values in a different order still fails. The geometry is checked as geometry rather than against numbers copied out of a run: the light view's rotation is orthonormal, three unit rows mutually perpendicular, and all eight corners of the scene box transformed through view times projection with XNA's own Matrix.Multiply and Vector3.Transform land inside the light's clip volume. Fitted rather than merely contained: the corners reach at least 0.95 of the frustum on both screen axes, measured at 0.998 for a large scene and 0.980 for a unit box, and the depth range is exactly zero to one. A different light direction produces a different view. Three planted defects fail: a quality that never reaches the size lookup, a projection computed from the identity, and a light that always points down. The shadow map object's own state -- size, filter radius and quality read back from its tier, and a depth bias that round-trips -- is verified on HEADLESS at 2048px

entries.operation: The .cnj compile front end, and the dependency lists a build system needs
entries.evidence: a .cnj document authored here from its own specification -- so what the runtime decodes is evidence about the compiler rather than CNA agreeing with itself -- compiles into a .cnb the runtime package reads back with every key's position, value and continuity exactly as the JSON declared, and with the loop kinds it named. The content name defaults to the document stem and honours an override. A document naming a PNG sidecar reports both files in AbsorbedFiles, which is the dependency set a build system watches, and the four texels the PNG carried arrive through the compiler unchanged. An unsupported asset type, a missing sidecar and a missing document are each refused with CNA's own IO result rather than a message match, which is what distinguishes CNA refusing from this package refusing first. It lives in cna-ts-content because it takes filesystem paths

entries.operation: The Guide's two asynchronous screens, and CNA's own answers to them
entries.evidence: Guide.BeginShowMessageBox and Guide.BeginShowKeyboardInput are the only genuinely asynchronous begin/end pairs in XNA, and both now work. A message box does not complete inside the Begin call and says so, carries the caller's async state untouched, makes Guide.IsVisible true, and holds the focus button XNA was given rather than a default. Answering it runs the continuation exactly once with the very result object Begin returned -- the IAsyncResult contract -- and EndShowMessageBox returns the button that was pressed; a second box with a different press returns that one instead, so the answer is not a constant. The keyboard input reports its title, description and starting text back from CNA, and a cancel makes EndShowKeyboardInput return null rather than an empty string, which is XNA's distinction. A second screen while one is pending is INVALID_STATE, and End before the answer is an error rather than a wait. Three planted defects fail: a dropped focus button, an End that accepts a foreign or incomplete result, and a continuation that fires twice. Nothing here fabricates a gamer, a sign-in or a peer: CNA draws the screen and answers it, which is the same deterministic injection the sensors and the camera use

entries.operation: The particle simulation, and the pure functions behind it
entries.evidence: cna_particle_system_step integrates one particle with no system, device or GPU, and cna_particle_system_random is the deterministic generator the emitter draws from -- so the simulation is checked against arithmetic rather than against numbers recorded from a run. Gravity of -10 over half a second gives velocity -5 and position -2.5 exactly, an axis with no gravity is unchanged, and the age advances by the step. Two half steps and one whole step both reach velocity -10 but land in different places, which is what shows the elapsed time reaching a stepwise integrator rather than being ignored; a zero step changes nothing; and Step returns a new particle rather than mutating the caller's. The same seed always draws the same value and different seeds draw different ones. The system itself round-trips its emitter settings through a different route than they went in, reports its capacity, and says whether it is simulating on the GPU and why not -- forced onto the CPU here, which is how a game gets the same answer on every renderer. Three planted defects fail: a fixed step, a seed that never reaches the generator, and gravity that is always the default

entries.operation: Typed text, IME composition and the mouse cursor
entries.evidence: The one input family CNA pushes rather than letting a game poll, because composition is: an IME sends editing updates and candidate lists between the keystroke and the committed character, none of which fits a per-frame snapshot. XNA had no concept of any of it -- Keyboard.GetState reports physical keys, a different question from what the user typed the moment the layout is not US English. Driven through CNA's own _ext injection hooks, which is injection evidence rather than hardware evidence and says so. Nothing assumes ASCII: 'a', 'e-acute', two CJK ideographs and U+1F600 are delivered as six UTF-16 code units -- the emoji as the surrogate pair the platform actually sends -- and appending them rebuilds the text exactly; five characters from six code units. Composition text round-trips as UTF-8 with its selection start and length kept apart, and candidate lists keep their order, selection and orientation. A disposed subscription receives nothing further, and an exception thrown out of a handler is contained at the boundary rather than unwound into compiled C, with a later subscriber still running. Start, Stop, the typed start and the input rectangle all succeed while IsActive stays false, because HEADLESS has no window to start input on -- measured, not assumed. A cursor is an owned handle that closes and releases in that order and refuses after disposal. Three planted defects each fail the test: a code unit truncated to a byte, a composition Length reported as its Start, and an unsubscribe that never reaches CNA

entries.operation: VideoPlayer.GetTexture borrowed frame projection and its decode identity
entries.evidence: cna_video_player_get_frame_ext's monotonic decode generation is what made a safe projection possible: GetTexture now hands back a non-owning Texture2D over the player's own frame, returns the same object while the generation is unchanged, and retires it the moment anything else touches the player -- the exact window CNA says the handle is valid for. entries.operation: Windowed Linux qualification: real GPU pixels through the public XNA drawing path
entries.evidence: against an OPENGLES3/SDL3 CNA library under Xvfb, a RenderTarget2D cleared to (12, 34, 56, 255) through GraphicsDevice.Clear reads back all sixteen texels exactly, the renderer reports itself as OPENGLES3 with a 16384-texel limit and 0x7ffff capability flags, a stock BasicEffect pass applies for real rather than returning the HEADLESS not-supported branch, and 60 and 600 SpriteBatch frames run without drift. Opt-in through CNA_WINDOWED_LIBRARY, and it skips with a reason where no windowed library or display exists

entries.operation: Windowed qualification across three renderers, with GameWindow and adapter state
entries.evidence: The windowed suite now runs against every renderer it is pointed at and has been run against three: OPENGLES3, SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE, all ABI 0.21 and all under Xvfb. Each reports its own identity, capability flags and texture limit; each applies a stock BasicEffect for real; each runs 60 and 600 frames. GameWindow is exercised where HEADLESS cannot reach it: a title written and read back and restored, a native handle that stays a bigint, a screen device name, an orientation, and AllowUserResizing flipped and restored. Client bounds are measured rather than assumed, because the renderers disagree honestly -- OPENGLES3 and SDL_RENDERER report the 320x240 the manager requested, SOFTWARE reports 0x0 because it presents through a surface -- so what is asserted is that a renderer reporting a client area reports the requested one. SDL_RENDERER and SOFTWARE produce the exact sixteen render-target texels; OPENGLES3 no longer does, and that regression is asserted as measured rather than skipped, so its repair fails the test. See docs/upstream-cna-findings.md item 7

entries.operation: Browser GamePad: connection, capabilities, buttons, thumbsticks and triggers
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser-input.mjs drives GamePad.GetState/GetCapabilities from inside an ordinary XNA Update in headless Chromium. With no controller attached all four PlayerIndex slots report IsConnected false rather than an invented device; with a Gamepad API device emulated at the browser boundary -- the integration point SDL3's Emscripten joystick driver actually reads -- the capability table, A and D-pad button states, both thumbstick axes with CNA's Y-inversion, the analog left trigger and an advancing PacketNumber all arrive, and releasing returns every one of them to zero. SetVibration reports false, because the browser's standard mapping exposes no rumble to SDL. Three planted defects -- swapped thumbsticks, an always-connected capability table and a previous-position that reports the current one -- each fail exactly one of these tests

entries.operation: Browser TouchPanel: the touch collection and XNA's press/move/release states
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser-input.mjs dispatches real Chromium touch events and reads TouchPanel.GetState from inside Update. Before the first finger there is no touch device at all, which is distinct from a device with nothing on it. A press arrives as TouchLocationState.Pressed with no previous location, the next frame is Moved at the same point, a move keeps the identifier and reports the press position as its previous one, a second finger is Pressed while the first stays Moved, and lifting reports Released exactly once before the collection empties. The XNA enumerator visits the same identifiers in the same order as the indexer

entries.operation: CNB curves and animation clips in a browser
entries.evidence: the same two schemas over the WebAssembly backend, and the one that settles a wasm32 convention with evidence: cna_curve_key_collection_add takes CNA_CurveKey **by value**, and cna_cnb_encode_animation_clip takes a descriptor holding a pointer to an array of descriptors each holding a pointer to an array of 48-byte keyframes. entries.operation: CNB in a browser: the same compiled-content API, on the WebAssembly backend

The container primitives agree across backends too: the CRC-32C check value and the magic are the same C routines either side

entries.operation: CNB media in a browser, including a measured sound-effect duration
entries.evidence: the same three schemas over the WebAssembly backend. The browser artifact is built with SDL3 audio rather than NULL, so this is where the sound effect's duration is actually measurable: a quarter second of 8 kHz mono PCM16 encoded to .cnb, decoded back and turned into an XNA SoundEffect reports exactly 250 ms and 2,500,000 ticks, which is arithmetic on the frame count and therefore exact evidence that the samples and the rate both survived. Both loop numbers, the sample bytes, and the song and video descriptions are asserted as on Node

entries.operation: CNB model in a browser: the same schema, on the WebAssembly backend
entries.evidence: a page builds a model with CnbModelData, encodes it with CNA's own writer and decodes it back, asserting the same values the Node suite asserts: both bone parents and both transforms, the part's stride and its exact vertex and index payloads through wasm32 memory, two named texture slots beside a third left empty, the mesh's parent bone and part list, all three skeleton matrix sets kept apart by their own diagonals, and the baked light. The structure layouts are measured by the same Emscripten probe as the rest, never hand-written. A planted defect that ignored the skeleton matrix-set identity fails this test; a second, which returned zero for every bone parent, passed until the test was strengthened to sample the root bone as well as the child -- so the gate is known to be able to fail for both

entries.operation: CNB's writers produce identical bytes on both backends
entries.evidence: the content-pipeline boundary claims a .cnb built in a build script and one built in a page are the same bytes. A browser page builds the same 52-byte payload and the same 326-byte container from the same calls, and the test compares the payload against the exact little-endian layout the desktop ABI produces rather than against the page agreeing with itself. The read-limits structure crosses through a wasm32 layout measured by an Emscripten probe, not a handwritten one
